blueprint_inputs.why: Minutes scale every counting stat and are only known as a distribution.
Status of the player and key teammates at decision time.
Count distribution shape controls tail probabilities across rungs.
Role and shot attempt volume for Player single-game counting stat.
Blowout minutes loss cuts the right tail.
Shooting luck mean reversion for Player single-game counting stat.
Price path and line moves reveal news and give the executable price at the decision time.
Wording decides whether OT/DNP/postponement count and therefore what is being predicted.
Sharp book prices are an independent estimate of the same distribution; the disagreement is the signal.
Rung correlation and implied distribution check.
Reliability curve by price bucket and side shows how far to shade model probabilities for this market family.
Liquidity rank of the rung scales how much edge to discount for better-arbitraged main lines.
Taker-side prints before moves are a candidate informed-flow signal and set realistic fill assumptions.
Settled values (and their timing) are the labels for calibration and need reconciling with the named stat source.
Post-game stat corrections can flip a rung sitting exactly at the threshold, so settlement timing and source matter.

unreg:all_star_weekend_events.blueprint_mechanism: Count = minutes times per-minute rate, modulated by opponent and game state and with distribution shape from overdispersion. Rates differ by stat (threes: attempts times make probability; steals/blocks: low-count Poisson-like; FT: attempts times FT%). Availability of teammates and minutes dominate the variance.
